How woodcocks evolved to be the weird cousins of their family
items.summary: A woodcock is an odd little bird with a long, skinny bill and a plump, chunky body that's shaped like an American football. It mostly hangs out near the ground, but it does a mating display in which it makes a buzzy, tweeting call and then takes off zigzagging across the sky. The woodcock stands out from most of the members of its family, the sandpipers. The majority of sandpiper species are champion migrators that traverse thousands of miles every year, but many woodcock species and their closest cousins, the snipes, have evolved to migrate shorter distances. Some island-dwelling species of woodcocks and snipes don't migrate at all.

Ronnie Rivers put together a sensational performance — in just one drive. Rivers had 15 touches on a single drive in the Rams' 34-6 win over the Arizona Cardinals and became the first player in the last 25 years to reach that number on one possession, per ESPN . Rivers accounted for every touch on the Rams' final drive, a 17-play possession that started with 12:15 left in the fourth quarter. He gained 81 yards on the 15 carries, with his longest runs going for 16, 13 and 11 yards. The drive burned 10 minutes and 15 seconds off the clock and carried the Rams to the two-minute warning, effectively ending the game. From there, Matthew Stafford only needed to kneel the ball out.

When Tatis came to the Padres, he was a solid prospect that San Diego managed to flip veteran pitcher James Shields for. That trade with the Chicago White Sox quickly became one of the most lopsided in MLB history. Tatis became a star in San Diego, slugging 42 homers in 2021. Meanwhile, Shields made just 76 starts for Chicago before retiring. Tatis' 2026 season started off rather unfortunately. The right fielder started the season going 55 games (207 at-bats) without a home run. It was the longest drought of his career. It's the second-longest drought to start a season by any player in history who had previously hit 40-plus homers. Tatis' power seemed to go dormant, until it didn't.

The Celtics' 42-9 margin at the end of the first period was the third-largest by a team in a quarter in the shot clock era. The Boston Celtics rolled to a 42-9 lead in the opening quarter of the contest. That marked Boston's largest lead at the end of the first period in franchise history. It gets even worse for the Mavericks. The Celtics' 42-9 scoring margin was the best from any team in the league in any quarter since 1987, when the Los Angeles Lakers outscored the Sacramento Kings 40-4 in the first quarter, according to ESPN . It was also the third-best mark by a team in a quarter in the shot clock era, which started back in 1954.

Raiders tight end Brock Bowers didn't play in the second half of Sunday's 21-13 loss to the Seahawks and there was no immediate word on when he'd back in the lineup. He was ruled out ahead of the third quarter and head coach Klint Kubiak said after the game that he did not have any idea about the severity of the injury. Kubiak said that Bowers will be re-evaluated on Monday. The Raiders play the Broncos in Week 11 and more word about his availability for that contest should come in the next few days.

(AP) — It is common for UConn to see games decided by 18 or more points. It's rare when the Huskies have been on the losing end of those contests. Seventh-ranked Louisville handed the No. 4 Huskies a rare 69-51 rout on Sunday night. Joe Burrow has accomplished something that had not been done for over 20 years. CALGARY, Alberta (AP) — Cody Fajardo threw two touchdown passes and ran for two scores and the Edmonton Elks won their record 15th Grey Cup title and first in 11 years, beating the Montreal Alouettes 37-30 on Sunday night.Selected the game MVP, Fajardo was 16 of 22 for 199 yards with an interception. Montreal had a second straight Grey Cup setback. The Als lost 25-17 last year to the Saskatchewan Roughriders. Vincent Blanchard's 42-yard field goal with 2:14 to play put Edmonton ahead 34-27. Montreal turned the ball over on downs with 1:40 remaining, setting up Blanchard's 43-yarder with 1:05 to go. Jose Maltos Diaz connected from 50 yards out with a second left for Montreal.

The University of Akron beat Georgetown in the men's soccer Big East Tournament final and advanced to the NCAA Tournament. Check out how Akron won. Sam Bunch scored a walk-off goal in overtime to lift No. 3 seed Akron to a 1-0 win over No. 1 seed Georgetown in the conference tournament championship match Sunday, Nov. 15, at the Maryland SportsPlex in Boyds, Md. Bunch's strike in the 93rd minute lifted Akron (13-1-4), ranked No. 4 in the latest national coaches poll, to its 16th overall conference title and first conference tournament crown since joining the Big East in 2023. The Zips won 15 Mid-American Conference Tournament championships from 1998-2018.

Birkenhead became the birthplace of basketball in England when the sport arrived in the town in 1892. It was during a business trip to Canada that the president of the town's YMCA, C J Proctor, first came across the game and introduced the sport at Birkenhead's YMCA gym on Merseyside when he returned. Invented just a year earlier, the game involved bouncing a ball into a fruit basket on a 10-foot-tall (3.05m) pole. Now 134 years on, two fathers, from Wirral, have launched a project with the hope of bringing professional standard courts and a 3,000 seat arena to the town where it all began.

Spain says nearly 2,200 migrants reached the Canary Islands in two days, with most arriving on the small island of El Hierro. Nearly 2,200 migrants have reached Spain’s Canary Islands by boat over the past two days, Spain’s maritime rescue service said on Sunday. The archipelago off northwest Africa is a major entry point for migrants, mainly from West Africa, attempting the dangerous Atlantic crossing in makeshift boats. More than 13,000 of the just over 28,000 people who arrived in Spain by sea between January and the end of October landed in the Canary Islands, according to the Interior Ministry.

IPL teams always have the option to release a player before a season starts, and here's everything you'll need to know about the process. Released players are not automatically entered into the auction and must register for it. Initially dedicated to grumbles, the show's unique format was soon expanded to include praise. Speaking at Monday's unveiling, Praise or Grumble's longest-running presenter Andy Giddings said: "It's not about who sits in the chair, it's about the people who get involved. That's why it's still going strong after 40 years."

Credit freeze, fraud alert or identity monitoring? After a data breach, the right identity theft protection depends on what information was exposed. All estimates of human spaceflight on Starship should be taken with a gigantic grain of salt. However, it raises other questions. The short answer is pretty simple: If SpaceX prioritizes human spaceflight on Starship, it could happen reasonably quickly. The longer answer becomes more complicated and depends on what one means by human spaceflight. The first people to fly on Starship probably won’t launch from Earth, or land here. Rather, they will probably be NASA’s lunar astronauts. So there are different timelines for humans flying aboard Starship and landing on Earth.

Michigan Football took another major step back in ESPN’s SP+ rankings following the loss to Oregon. Here’s where things stand with two weeks left: For those of you who might be new to SP+, it's an advanced metric that takes into account a team's offensive, defensive, and special teams efficiencies. It combines all three metrics into one uniform metric that predicts how many points a given team would defeat (or lose to) the "average" college football team by on a neutral field. In other words, it's a metric designed to look at how "good" teams really are at different aspects of the game rather than ranking them purely on their resumes.

All 32 NHL teams saw increases in valuation, per CNBC. The Mammoth's total franchise value, per the report, now sits at $1.85 billion, making them the 27th-most-valuable team in the league. That's up from $1.6 billion the previous year, and significantly higher than the the $1.2 billion Smith Entertainment Group reportedly paid for the team in 2024. That type of growth wasn't exclusive to the Mammoth. In fact, all 32 NHL teams increased in value, and the Mammoth were tied for the third-least growth of them all. Ken "Bulldog" Sanders, a standout on the first three Milwaukee Brewers teams who stayed in the area after his playing days, died at 85. The St. Louis-born Sanders spent 10 seasons in Major League Baseball, including the first three seasons of the Milwaukee Brewers' existence from 1970 through 1972, when he had a 2.21 ERA and 61 saves. He continued living in the Milwaukee area after his time in the big leagues. "Bulldog" – a nickname bestowed by former Brewers manager Dave Bristol – led the American League with 31 saves in 1971 and posted a 1.91 ERA and 1.064 WHIP, even earning MVP votes that season.

The Ballymacombs More Woman was discovered near Bellaghy - and suffered a deliberate decapitation. For more than 2,000 years, the remains of an Iron Age woman laid undiscovered in bogland - her story unlikely to ever be told. But when archaeologists unearthed human bones in 2023, it led to an unprecedented effort in Northern Ireland to find out who they belonged to - and what had happened to that person. Now a coroner's investigation has been held at the Ulster Museum in Belfast to establish the truth behind the Ballymacombs More Woman.

The Florida Vibe drew a packed crowd as they were introduced as Pensacola's latest professional sports team. The Florida Vibe were set to be introduced on their future home field at Blue Wahoos Stadium . But with rain in the forecast for the 5 p.m. event, they moved it to the Hancock Whitney Club, which sits mostly covered above the concourse on the left side of the stadium. Fans packed the exclusive area, filling every seat and overflowing into every inch of deck. Quite the introduction for the latest professional sports team to move to Pensacola. The Vibe are members of the Professional Softball League, and will start playing at Blue Wahoos Stadium in June.

This Storyville film talks to Peter Sichel, who fled Nazi Germany, then became the CIA’s first station chief in Berlin. Plus: Stacey & Joe go camping. Here’s what to watch this evening 10pm, BBC Four Some people are blessed with interesting lives, others are cursed with them. It’s hard to say which category Peter Sichel falls into, but he lived quite a story and managed to tell it in this documentary, shortly before his death, aged 102. As a child, he fled Nazi Germany for the US. He later landed at the CIA and played a role in some of the late-20th century’s pivotal events. His critique of US foreign policy during that era is forensic and fascinating. Phil Harrison

The remains of a top Australian racehorse that died of colic on Monday were found at a public rubbish tip. The body of a top Australian racehorse has been found dumped in a skip bin, hours after its trainer revealed the horse had died from colic. In a video shared online, only two weeks after So You Are raced in the Melbourne Cup, the deceased racehorse appeared to be lying in a large metal bin surrounded by other household rubbish in Sydney. Trainer Bjorn Baker - who shared news of the horse's death from colic on Monday - has said he was "deeply distressed" by the video, and called for a "full explanation".

The Suica penguin has been a familiar presence on prepaid transit cards for more than 20 years. Its imminent retirement has prompted a wave of nostalgia. For more than two decades, train commuters in Japan have had a faithful companion on their daily journeys: the Suica penguin. But the little black-and-white bird will soon take its last ride. One of Japan’s largest rail operators adopted the penguin as the mascot for its prepaid smart cards, known as Suica cards, in 2001. On the cards, the penguin is smiling and waving as it walks.
